A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cache-aware MoE routing work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original WikiText, MMLU and GSM8K evaluations, mobile throughput measurements, expert-selection analyses and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds oracle-caching comparisons, broader cache-size tests, router-selection analysis and deployment robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The Max-Rank, cumulative-threshold and additive cache-prior procedures remain unchanged, including preservation of original mixing weights and optional top-J protection. The appendix's learned two-layer MLP variant also already existed. Renaming Prior to Cache-Prior and expanding explanations do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: WikiText-2, MMLU and GSM8K remain the benchmark suite. The limited scenario expansion is the explicit evaluation of short 40–60-token and long 300–400-token on-device prompts in Section 4.5 and Appendix F, adding contrasted input-length conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds Belady's optimal fixed-routing cache policy as an evaluated oracle comparator in Figures 10–11. This substantially strengthens comparison beyond LRU and the existing routing baselines. Original Routing and Cache-Prior otherwise match the former LRU and Prior labels.

E3.justification: New protocols sweep cache sizes from one expert to all experts and select lambda under 1%, 5% and 10% perplexity limits, alongside controlled initialization and prompt-length experiments. v2 also corrects the main-text mobile cache sizes from 45/30 to 30/45 experts for the 4-bit/8-bit deployments; v1's appendix already stated 30/45, so this does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds optimal second-expert selection analysis, oracle and broader cache-size comparisons, empty-versus-random cache initialization tests, and throughput analyses by cache hit rate and prompt length. It removes v1 Appendix C's LRU insertion-order ablation. The smaller-cache, top-J, logit-range and learned-prior analyses were already present.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 9 adds plus/minus values to cache lifetimes without defining the reported statistic. Section 4.1 newly identifies trade-off results as single-pass deterministic point estimates. The existing ten-run mobile boxplots remain; an increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover oracle caching, router optimality, cache sizes, initialization and prompt-dependent throughput. Existing values also change: v1 Table 2 becomes v2 Figure 9, where at matching reported cache sizes and lambda=0.5, Qwen's Prior lifetime/miss rate changes from 111 tokens/7% to 58 tokens/16%, and DeepSeek's from 188 tokens/3% to 76 tokens/7%.

T1.justification: Equation 8 corrects the cumulative-sum term from G(x)[r_i] to G(x)[r_j], matching the summation index and existing pseudocode. The principal mathematical definitions and routing equations remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The training-free routing and approximately twofold mobile speedup claims remain. The abstract and conclusion add a central claim of exceeding the optimal fixed-routing cache bound through controlled expert substitution, quantify cache reductions and predictive-performance costs, and emphasize granular architectures' cache efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 4.7 adds interpretations involving granularity, expansion rate, top-K and shared experts. New discussion explains possible prompt-length throughput effects and router suboptimality, while Section 4.8 and Appendix G identify excessive cached-expert reuse at large lambda as a limitation. The regularization explanation is also more explicitly qualified as a hypothesis.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies hyperparameter sweep grids, including 50 equally spaced values for threshold and cache-prior sweeps. Table 1 adds int4 memory-footprint ranges, and new experiments disclose their cache and lambda configurations. Core preprocessing, few-shot settings, llama.cpp, Android and memory-locking information were already documented.

R1.justification: A substantial Expert Caching subsection distinguishes conventional lossless caching from lossy approaches such as Adapt-MoE and HOBBIT, positioning the method against the oracle bound. Added references cover Belady, Fiddler, SwapMoE, EdgeMoE, fine-grained MoE scaling and nucleus sampling, substantially extending the earlier positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experimental setup and implementation are separated, appendix material is reorganized, and worked baseline explanations are added. Terminology is standardized from Prior/LRU to Cache-Prior/Original Routing.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, revises diagrams, captions and legends, expands Table 1, and presents the former cache-lifetime table as Figure 9. Numerous analytical figures and a baseline schematic are added; existing plots are relocated and the LRU insertion-order figure is removed.

improvement.justification: The oracle comparator and broader robustness and deployment tests strengthen validation beyond v1's LRU-based comparisons, while clearer explanations and sweep details improve usability. Reporting problems temper these gains: Section 4.6 retains the 5–9× lifetime claim despite revised Figure 9 values, and the new blanket claim of over 50% fewer misses with under 0.1% downstream accuracy loss is not uniformly supported by Figure 6. Mixtral's GSM8K accuracy falls from roughly 59% to 57% when misses are approximately halved. The empirical case improves, but the quantitative claims need reconciliation.
